data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Reliability gain is genuine if and only if the panel-plus-checklist demonstrates the same or better performance on held-out tasks drawn from a different distribution than the training distribution of the checklist, distinguishing causal understanding from memorized compliance.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the domain has no stable causal structure (e.g., purely random or adversarial outcomes), no checklist can generalize, and the expert's intuition may be equally unreliable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the held-out distribution shift is so large that it renders the expert's intuition equally invalid, neither approach will show reliable performance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is updated in response to the distribution shift before evaluation, this test cannot distinguish genuine understanding from adaptive compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance that tracks the right answer relies on the checklist being a lookup table for the training distribution. Causal understanding via the checklist generalizes because the checklist encodes the generative structure of the task domain. A held-out task distribution shift probes generalization: if the panel's performance drops to chance or below the expert's, the checklist was merely tracking the right answer via distribution-specific heuristics; if it holds, the checklist captures causal structure that the panel can apply beyond the training distribution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
